facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Net debt rose from USD 2,811.76 million at 30 June 2025 to USD 5,022.58 million at 31 March 2026 because the ARKA acquisition was funded with debt, then fell to USD 4,556.67 million at 30 September 2026 as EBITDA grew and cash built. Net leverage on trailing EBITDA moved from 2.91x to 4.63x, then to 4.01x at 30 June 2026 and 3.69x at 30 September 2026. Part of the improvement is mechanical: the acquisition debt was in place by mid-March 2026 while ARKA earnings enter the trailing total only from the closing on 9 March 2026, so each further quarter adds ARKA earnings to the denominator and lowers the ratio without any debt repayment. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66, 79; 10-Q_2026-03-31_caci-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C5

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Two points cut against the not-like-for-like reading. If ARKA earned little before its closing, a full-year figure would barely lower leverage, and if cash interest in the December 2026 quarter, when the semi-annual coupons fall due, comes in near a quarter of the trailing total, the overstatement of cover is small. Deleveraging is also real: net debt fell USD 153.08 million in the September 2026 quarter and the issuer guides to free cash flow of at least USD 900 million in fiscal 2027. The reading would be confirmed if working capital keeps absorbing cash, as in the September 2026 quarter, or if the receivables programme lapses at the end of its stated term on 18 December 2026 without renewal. rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions are not printed in any document read; the annual report and the September 2026 quarterly report state only that the company was in compliance with its financial covenants, and one earlier quarterly report names a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio. This restricts every leverage and cover ratio to a reported-figure reading, not a covenant test. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement. - The earnings of ARKA before its closing on 9 March 2026 are not printed and the annual report states that pro forma results are not material, so trailing EBITDA holds about seven months of ARKA against full acquisition debt and no pro forma leverage or cover can be stated for any period after 2026-03-31. Severity Medium. Action: obtain management pro forma figures. - EBITDA for fiscal 2024 is not calculable because the issuer's EBITDA adds depreciation held within direct costs and the sources do not state it for that year; this removes fiscal 2024 from the EBITDA series, the ratios and the revenue and EBITDA chart. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the fiscal 2024 reconciliation. - Depreciation held within direct costs is not stated for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and for fiscal 2024, and no release for the second quarter is in the sources, so second quarter EBITDA is derived from nine months less the first and third quarters. Severity Low. Action: obtain the second quarter release. - Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed; only the aggregate of unamortized debt discount, premium and issuance costs is, so instrument rows carry principal and one financing cost row reconciles to total debt. Severity Low. Action: none needed beyond the reconciliation. - The margin over SOFR for each facility is not printed because it depends on the consolidated total net leverage ratio, no floor is stated, and the relative priority among the secured facilities is not stated; rank 1 is used for the secured group because the annual report calls them senior secured and the notes subordinated. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement. - The revolving commitment at 30 June 2025 is not stated, so undrawn capacity at that date is not supplied; undrawn capacity at 31 December 2025 is calculated from the stated absence of borrowings and a revolver of USD 2,000.0 million. Severity Low. Action: obtain the earlier credit agreement terms. - The September 2026 quarterly report prints no debt maturity ladder, so the ladder is drawn at 30 June 2026 and amortisation since then is not rolled forward. Severity Low. Action: obtain the current ladder. - Interest income is not separately stated because the income statement shows interest expense and other, net; gross profit, cost of goods sold, maintenance and growth capital expenditure, and a split of exceptional items by quarter are not presented. Acquisition-related costs are stated only as USD 22.5 million for fiscal 2026 and USD 14.1 million for fiscal 2025. Severity Low. Action: none; the issuer's own lines are kept. - Lines printed as a dash or not printed in a cash flow period, such as the gain on divestiture of business, other operating and investing items and deferred financing costs, are carried as not supplied and never as zero. Severity Low. Action: none. - Cash flow statements are cumulative in the quarterly reports, so the cash flow table carries the first quarter, six months and nine months and no discrete second, third or fourth quarter; the income statement carries discrete quarters. Severity Low. Action: derive discrete quarters only if needed. - The second, third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2025 are printed as comparatives in later reports but are not carried as columns; only the prior-year comparative needed for each trailing figure is carried. Severity Low. Action: add columns if a quarterly year-on-year series is required. - Foreign cash of USD 92.7 million at 30 September 2026 is held in the United Kingdom and the Netherlands and is not immediately available to fund U.S. operations without repatriation, and collections of USD 160.719 million held for the receivables purchaser are recorded as a current liability; neither is deducted from cash in net debt. Severity Medium. Action: treat the net debt figure with this margin. - The receivables purchase agreement term is stated as ending 18 December 2026 in the annual report and the two earlier quarterly reports but is not restated in the September 2026 quarterly report, so renewal is not established; sold receivables of USD 349.999 million sit at the USD 350.0 million maximum. Severity Medium. Action: confirm renewal. - The fiscal year change to 31 December means the next report covers a six-month transition period ending 31 December 2026, after the cutoff, so period labels and comparability will change. Severity Low. Action: relabel periods when that report is available.

facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a solid profile is that fiscal 2026 cash flow was helped by items that may not repeat: deferred income taxes swung by USD 172.45 million, income tax expense exceeded cash taxes paid by USD 75.38 million, and sales of receivables added USD 44.62 million to operating cash flow, so free cash flow could fall short of the issuer's guidance of at least USD 900 million for fiscal 2027 if those effects reverse; organic growth has slowed to 2.1% and the fixed-price share is rising. The view would weaken if the September 2026 collection days of 59 rise further, if the receivables programme lapses on 18 December 2026, or if a continuing resolution delays awards against the small funded backlog. It would strengthen if free cash flow reaches the guided floor while net leverage keeps falling from 3.69x and the executed debt documents show tight distribution limits. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Federal demand is large and broad: revenue of USD 9,567.78 million in fiscal 2026 came from agencies across defense, intelligence and civilian missions, and USD 34.0 billion of backlog gives visibility, so a single program loss does not threaten debt service. Cash conversion is high: free cash flow was 62.65% of EBITDA and the issuer guides to at least USD 900 million in fiscal 2027, which funds deleveraging. Liquidity is large against near-term maturities: USD 1,674.39 million against USD 46.75 million of amortisation. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditures of 1.11% of revenue, so cash flow is not absorbed by plant. Financial policy is conservative on distributions: no dividend has been paid and repurchases fell to USD 17.08 million in fiscal 2026. facts.label: Revenue durability
facts.text: Revenue grew 12.64% in fiscal 2025 and 10.89% in fiscal 2026, with organic growth of 7.2% in fiscal 2026 and 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter. The Department of War supplied 53.6% of revenue, the Intelligence Community 24.6% and federal civilian agencies 17.4%, and the ten largest contracts were 22.5% of revenue. The revenue is predictable in aggregate but concentrated and budget-dependent: continuing resolutions and the shutdown from 1 October 2025 to 12 November 2025 delay awards, and only USD 6.2 billion of USD 34.0 billion of backlog is funded. The credit implication is that a funding delay moves cash flow before it moves covenants or ratings. facts.label: Margin resilience
facts.text: The EBITDA margin was 11.2% in fiscal 2025, 12.3% in fiscal 2026 and 13.3% in the September 2026 quarter. Margins can be defended against volume pressure because labor is variable with contract volume, but an adverse fixed-price outcome would not be passed on. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is high: the company states that it competes against many firms, some larger, with no dominant competitor and a relatively small share of its addressable market, so re-competes can be lost, which would show first in backlog and awards. Non-traditional entrants in cloud, cyber and satellite operations raise entry pressure, and agencies that perform services for themselves are an indirect substitute. Buyer power is strong because the government sets contract terms and can terminate for convenience, although terminations have been rare. Supplier power sits mainly in cleared labor, where competition for skilled staff is intense and limits cost control. The credit effect is limited pricing power and a reliance on win rates and contract mix. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Policy is the dominant external factor. Defense appropriations of USD 838.7 billion were enacted for the government's 2026 fiscal year and mandatory funding of about USD 156 billion for defense became available outside annual appropriations, which supports demand regardless of continuing resolutions. Economic exposure is mainly interest rates, since most debt is floating. The credit effect is demand support from defense funding against timing risk from shutdowns, which interrupted government operations from 1 October to 12 November 2025. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths: federal scale, cash conversion of 62.65% of EBITDA, low capital intensity, large liquidity and no dividend history. Weaknesses: concentration, fixed-price drift, acquisition leverage, goodwill-heavy assets and a capped receivables programme. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: defense funding and the guided free cash flow of at least USD 900 million, which could pay down debt. Threats that could weaken it: a prolonged shutdown or continuing resolution, a large fixed-price overrun, integration problems at ARKA and a rise in floating rates. Cost and capex flexibility is a support, with capital expenditures of 1.11% of revenue and a labor-based cost base. Margin stability is average because the mix is shifting toward fixed-price work. Free cash flow stability is average because fiscal 2026 had tax and receivable-sale help. Liquidity is a support at USD 1,674.39 million. Ability to refinance is average because recent issuance is strong but ratings and covenants are not supplied. Financial policy and governance is average: distributions are minimal but acquisitions are debt-funded and structural governance is not established. The trend is improving leverage from a high of 4.63x at 31 March 2026 to 3.69x; the main constraints are concentration and fixed-price risk; the key missing datapoints are covenant levels, ratings, ownership detail and ARKA pro forma earnings. facts.text: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to USD 10,700 million to USD 10,900 million and guides to free cash flow of at least USD 900 million, supported by a 2.0x book-to-bill in the quarter and defense funding; that supports deleveraging if working capital cooperates. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a continuing resolution or shutdown, as occurred from 1 October 2025, that delays task order awards while a fixed-price program overruns. The first operational break is slower revenue conversion from a backlog of which only USD 6.2 billion is funded, with the overrun cutting the margin. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA and weaker cash conversion; a fall of 1.00 percentage points in the margin on trailing revenue removes USD 97.55 million of EBITDA, lifts net leverage to 4.01x and cuts cover to 3.88x against the annualised interest charge, while collection days of 59 and a capped receivables programme absorb cash. The liquidity consequence is a draw on the revolver from USD 1,674.39 million of liquidity; the leverage consequence is a return to the level of 30 June 2026. Management levers are repurchases, which are small, acquisitions, which can be paused, and capital expenditures of only 1.11% of revenue. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because liquidity is 35.82 times scheduled amortisation, but covenant headroom is not established. Observable triggers are collection days above 59, a book-to-bill below 1.0x and free cash flow below USD 900 million. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, CACI presents an adequate business profile supported by federal scale, broad agency demand, cash conversion of 62.65% of EBITDA and large liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, a rising fixed-price share and acquisition debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because fiscal 2026 benefited from tax timing and receivable sales. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on federal funding continuity, leverage continuing to fall from 3.69x and the November 2030 revolver and Term Loan maturities. The primary downside path is a budget delay combined with a fixed-price overrun. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, ratings, the proxy statement and ARKA pro forma earnings. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied CACI filings and earnings releases are sufficient to support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work for the period to 30 September 2026, but not covenant, rating or market-pricing conclusions. Reported debt, liquidity and earnings are therefore well sourced, while covenant headroom and ratings stay unverified for creditors.

The newest document is the quarterly report for the period ended 30 September 2026, signed 22 October 2026, which is 14 days before the as-of date. No executed credit agreement, indenture or amendment is in the set, so covenant levels and guarantor terms are not established; the filings report compliance but print no levels. The company also changed its fiscal year end to 31 December on 20 October 2026, so the next report covers a six-month transition period.

## Request

CACI INTERNATIONAL INC /DE/ (issuer id caci), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. The scope is the financial foundation from the seven supplied issuer documents: statements, debt, leverage, interest cover, liquidity and maturities. Money tables are in millions of US dollars and the statements are in thousands of US dollars as printed.

## Findings
### Bottom line

CACI's net leverage fell to 3.69x at 30 September 2026 from 4.63x at 31 March 2026, and liquidity covers near-term maturities, but both trailing ratios mix a full debt load with part-year earnings and interest. EBITDA holds only part of a year of ARKA, so leverage is overstated, while cash interest holds only part of a year of its debt cost, so interest cover is overstated.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C11; calculation C14

Liquidity is cash of USD 279.39 million plus an undrawn revolver of USD 1,395.00 million, against scheduled maturities of USD 46.75 million in the year to 30 June 2027 and no large maturity before fiscal 2031. Net debt of USD 4,556.67 million does not count USD 160.72 million of collections owed to the receivables purchaser, which the balance sheet carries as a current liability.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 20–21; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C5
### Key findings

Net debt rose from USD 2,811.76 million at 30 June 2025 to USD 5,022.58 million at 31 March 2026 because the ARKA acquisition was funded with debt, then fell to USD 4,556.67 million at 30 September 2026 as EBITDA grew and cash built. Net leverage on trailing EBITDA moved from 2.91x to 4.63x, then to 4.01x at 30 June 2026 and 3.69x at 30 September 2026. Part of the improvement is mechanical: the acquisition debt was in place by mid-March 2026 while ARKA earnings enter the trailing total only from the closing on 9 March 2026, so each further quarter adds ARKA earnings to the denominator and lowers the ratio without any debt repayment.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66, 79; 10-Q_2026-03-31_caci-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C5

EBITDA covered cash interest 5.60x over the last twelve months to 30 September 2026, against 6.67x at 30 June 2025, but cash interest paid understates the run-rate cost of the post-acquisition debt. The income statement charge for interest and other was USD 73.24 million in the September 2026 quarter against USD 46.17 million a year earlier; as an analyst sensitivity, annualised it is USD 292.96 million and gives cover of 4.21x on trailing EBITDA. The 2033 Notes pay semi-annually, so quarterly cash interest is uneven and the trailing figure holds only some of the new coupons.

Operating cash flow was USD 886.71 million in fiscal 2026 against USD 547.01 million in fiscal 2025, and issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 735.43 million, 62.65% of EBITDA. In the September 2026 quarter operating cash flow was USD 161.31 million against USD 171.07 million a year earlier because working capital absorbed cash, and issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 133.49 million against USD 142.96 million. Sales of receivables added USD 44.62 million to fiscal 2026 operating cash flow, and the programme is now at its ceiling, so it cannot add to cash flow from here.

Liquidity at 30 September 2026 was USD 1,674.39 million, made up of USD 279.39 million of cash and USD 1,395.00 million of undrawn revolver, with USD 605.00 million of the revolver drawn. Scheduled maturities are USD 46.75 million in the year to 30 June 2027 and USD 62.38 million in the following year; the revolver and Term Loan fall due in November 2030, inside the year to 30 June 2031 in which USD 1,706.75 million matures. Two balances that are not debt change how much cash is free. Collections held for the receivables purchaser rose from USD 110.13 million at 30 June 2026 to USD 160.72 million at 30 September 2026 and sit in other accrued liabilities. Current contract liabilities, the advances and deferred revenue that fund operations, rose from USD 190.40 million at 30 June 2025 to USD 294.06 million at 30 June 2026 and USD 337.94 million at 30 September 2026, and they unwind as work is performed.

Obligations outside the debt figure at 30 June 2026 are USD 483.02 million of operating lease liabilities, all of the company's leases being operating leases, USD 119.23 million of supplemental retirement savings plan obligations against USD 104.88 million of related assets, USD 6.97 million of unfunded post-retirement benefits, USD 8.32 million of contingent acquisition consideration and the receivables sold under the purchase agreement. The company reports no material off-balance-sheet financing, and the USD 42 million judgment in the Al Shimari action carries no recognised liability and was vacated on 21 October 2026, although the plaintiffs may seek Supreme Court review.

Every ratio uses the issuer's unadjusted EBITDA, which adds depreciation held within direct costs, USD 8.20 million more than the income statement charge in fiscal 2026. It does not add back the USD 22.5 million of acquisition-related costs expensed in fiscal 2026, so it is conservative on that item. The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA, net debt or leverage, and debt is measured at carrying value, USD 28.38 million below principal at 30 September 2026.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

Two points cut against the not-like-for-like reading. If ARKA earned little before its closing, a full-year figure would barely lower leverage, and if cash interest in the December 2026 quarter, when the semi-annual coupons fall due, comes in near a quarter of the trailing total, the overstatement of cover is small. Deleveraging is also real: net debt fell USD 153.08 million in the September 2026 quarter and the issuer guides to free cash flow of at least USD 900 million in fiscal 2027. The reading would be confirmed if working capital keeps absorbing cash, as in the September 2026 quarter, or if the receivables programme lapses at the end of its stated term on 18 December 2026 without renewal.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4, 21; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation C28
### Limitations

The filings state no adjusted EBITDA, net debt or leverage, so every ratio is calculated on the issuer's unadjusted EBITDA and carrying-value debt and is not a covenant figure, because the covenant definitions are not established.

Trailing figures at interim dates add the latest full year to the current stub and subtract the prior-year stub, and the second quarter of fiscal 2026 is derived because no release for that quarter is in the set.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-22_fy26-q3caci20260422ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C6; calculation C9

ARKA's earnings before its closing are not printed, so no pro forma leverage is stated, and the change of fiscal year end to 31 December means the next reported period is a six-month transition period ending 31 December 2026 that will not compare with a full quarter.

## Gaps

- Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions are not printed in any document read; the annual report and the September 2026 quarterly report state only that the company was in compliance with its financial covenants, and one earlier quarterly report names a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio. This restricts every leverage and cover ratio to a reported-figure reading, not a covenant test. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement.

- The earnings of ARKA before its closing on 9 March 2026 are not printed and the annual report states that pro forma results are not material, so trailing EBITDA holds about seven months of ARKA against full acquisition debt and no pro forma leverage or cover can be stated for any period after 2026-03-31. Severity Medium. Action: obtain management pro forma figures.

- EBITDA for fiscal 2024 is not calculable because the issuer's EBITDA adds depreciation held within direct costs and the sources do not state it for that year; this removes fiscal 2024 from the EBITDA series, the ratios and the revenue and EBITDA chart. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the fiscal 2024 reconciliation.

- Depreciation held within direct costs is not stated for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and for fiscal 2024, and no release for the second quarter is in the sources, so second quarter EBITDA is derived from nine months less the first and third quarters. Severity Low. Action: obtain the second quarter release.

- Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed; only the aggregate of unamortized debt discount, premium and issuance costs is, so instrument rows carry principal and one financing cost row reconciles to total debt. Severity Low. Action: none needed beyond the reconciliation.

- The margin over SOFR for each facility is not printed because it depends on the consolidated total net leverage ratio, no floor is stated, and the relative priority among the secured facilities is not stated; rank 1 is used for the secured group because the annual report calls them senior secured and the notes subordinated. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement.

- The revolving commitment at 30 June 2025 is not stated, so undrawn capacity at that date is not supplied; undrawn capacity at 31 December 2025 is calculated from the stated absence of borrowings and a revolver of USD 2,000.0 million. Severity Low. Action: obtain the earlier credit agreement terms.

- The September 2026 quarterly report prints no debt maturity ladder, so the ladder is drawn at 30 June 2026 and amortisation since then is not rolled forward. Severity Low. Action: obtain the current ladder.

- Interest income is not separately stated because the income statement shows interest expense and other, net; gross profit, cost of goods sold, maintenance and growth capital expenditure, and a split of exceptional items by quarter are not presented. Acquisition-related costs are stated only as USD 22.5 million for fiscal 2026 and USD 14.1 million for fiscal 2025. Severity Low. Action: none; the issuer's own lines are kept.

- Lines printed as a dash or not printed in a cash flow period, such as the gain on divestiture of business, other operating and investing items and deferred financing costs, are carried as not supplied and never as zero. Severity Low. Action: none.

- Cash flow statements are cumulative in the quarterly reports, so the cash flow table carries the first quarter, six months and nine months and no discrete second, third or fourth quarter; the income statement carries discrete quarters. Severity Low. Action: derive discrete quarters only if needed.

- The second, third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2025 are printed as comparatives in later reports but are not carried as columns; only the prior-year comparative needed for each trailing figure is carried. Severity Low. Action: add columns if a quarterly year-on-year series is required.

- Foreign cash of USD 92.7 million at 30 September 2026 is held in the United Kingdom and the Netherlands and is not immediately available to fund U.S. operations without repatriation, and collections of USD 160.719 million held for the receivables purchaser are recorded as a current liability; neither is deducted from cash in net debt. Severity Medium. Action: treat the net debt figure with this margin.

- The receivables purchase agreement term is stated as ending 18 December 2026 in the annual report and the two earlier quarterly reports but is not restated in the September 2026 quarterly report, so renewal is not established; sold receivables of USD 349.999 million sit at the USD 350.0 million maximum. Severity Medium. Action: confirm renewal.

- The fiscal year change to 31 December means the next report covers a six-month transition period ending 31 December 2026, after the cutoff, so period labels and comparability will change. Severity Low. Action: relabel periods when that report is available.

## Findings
### Bottom line

CACI is an NYSE-listed US national-security contractor with no sponsor identified, no dividend history and no creditor-adverse conduct in the filings, but serial debt-funded acquisitions and missing ownership and debt documents leave sponsor and governance risk at Medium for creditors.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 79, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C3

Revenue is 95.6% federal, so cash flow follows appropriations, and the mix is moving toward fixed-price work, which carries more cost-overrun risk; only USD 6.2 billion of USD 34.0 billion of backlog is funded. Principal debt rose from USD 2,942.63 million at 30 June 2025 to USD 4,931.13 million at 30 June 2026, mainly through the ARKA acquisition, while the USD 42 million Al Shimari judgment was vacated on 21 October 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 43, 86–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 20; calculation C3
### Key findings

- Customer concentration is high but spread across agencies. Federal contracts were 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue, of which the Department of War was 53.6%, the Intelligence Community 24.6% and federal civilian agencies 17.4%, and the ten largest contracts were 22.5% of revenue. A budget lapse or a termination for convenience therefore reaches cash flow across the group, although the company calls terminations rare and the agencies fund different missions, which limits the damage from the loss of one program.

- Backlog gives visibility but little of it is funded. Total backlog was USD 34.0 billion at 30 September 2026, up 0.3% on a year earlier, of which USD 6.2 billion, 18.2%, was funded; the rest depends on future appropriations, so a continuing resolution can delay conversion into revenue even in a quarter with a book-to-bill of 2.0x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4; calculation C6

- The contract mix is shifting toward fixed-price work, which raises margin volatility. Cost-plus-fee work fell to 52.8% of revenue in the September 2026 quarter from 60.5% a year earlier while fixed-price work rose to 33.2% from 26.7%; the contractor bears overruns on fixed-price work, so a cost overrun on one large program would reduce EBITDA and cash flow in a way cost-plus work would not.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 8

- Acquisitions are the behaviour that matters most for creditors, and they have been funded largely with debt. Acquisition spending was 2.97x operating cash flow in fiscal 2026 and 3.10x in fiscal 2025, net borrowings funded 75.9% of fiscal 2026 acquisition spending and 82.1% of fiscal 2025 spending, and principal debt rose by USD 1,988.50 million in the year, so the ARKA acquisition for USD 2,642.7 million left goodwill and intangibles at 72.40% of total assets and tangible equity negative at USD 4,094.75 million; recovery therefore rests on contract cash flows rather than hard assets.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 65–67, 79–81, 86–89; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C13

- Shareholder distributions are small and no sponsor exists to extract value, but buybacks remain authorised. CACI has never paid a cash dividend and states no intention to; repurchases in the cash flow statement were USD 161.49 million in fiscal 2024, USD 168.56 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 17.08 million in fiscal 2026, and USD 187.3 million of authorisation remained at 30 September 2026, so repurchases could resume from cash that would otherwise repay acquisition debt.

- Funding choices show terming-out and extension rather than creditor-adverse moves. Revolver borrowings were repaid with USD 1,000.0 million of 2033 Notes in June 2025 and USD 500.0 million more in March 2026, the credit facility maturity was extended on 25 November 2025, a USD 1,300.0 million bridge was left undrawn and ended at closing, and the company reports compliance with every covenant since inception. No waiver, exchange or priming transaction appears in the filings, but the executed debt documents that would show the capacity for one are not in the set.

- Governance structure cannot be assessed from the filings, and disclosure quality is adequate rather than strong. Board, compensation, ownership and related-party information is incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not in the set, so control rights and conflicts between shareholders and creditors are not established. The filings do show clean audit opinions from PricewaterhouseCoopers on the statements and on internal control, effective disclosure controls, ARKA elements left out of the first-year control assessment at 1.5% of assets and 1.0% of revenue, a board chair separate from the chief executive officer, and a policy that significant fixed-price contracts need the approval of at least two executives.

- Legal exposure fell on 21 October 2026. The USD 42 million Al Shimari judgment, for which no amount was recognised, was vacated and the case dismissed after the Supreme Court's June 2026 Cisco ruling, equal to 3.01% of undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,395.0 million; the plaintiffs may seek Supreme Court review and the related Abbass action remains stayed, so the effect on creditors is timing and headline risk rather than liquidity.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44, 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 21, 29–31; calculation C9
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower level is conduct: no dividend has ever been paid, repurchases fell to USD 17.08 million in fiscal 2026, the bridge was never drawn, covenants have been met since inception and net repayment of borrowings in the September 2026 quarter was USD 66.69 million. The level would move to Low if the proxy statement shows an independent board with no controlling holder and the credit agreement shows tight restricted payment and investment baskets. The strongest evidence for a higher level is eight acquisitions in three fiscal years, the largest funded mainly with new debt, with USD 187.3 million of repurchase authorisation still open. The level would move to High if a later report showed debt-funded repurchases or an amendment that loosened covenants to allow them.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 28, 46, 67, 81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12; calculation C10
### Limitations

- Board composition, independence, ownership and compensation are in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the structural side of the Medium level rests on conduct alone; a controlling holder or weak independence would raise it and a clean structure would lower it.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 103

- The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so legal capacity for restricted payments, investments and additional debt is not established and willingness is judged from actions only, which keeps the level from moving to Low.

- The filings do not split repurchases between the buyback programme and purchases that offset employee share issuance, so the repurchase amounts may overstate discretionary distributions by an amount that is not established.

- The sources end on 22 October 2026, before the December 2026 coupon dates, the end of the stated receivables purchase term and the six-month transition period, so conduct after those dates cannot change the level here.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 34

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

CACI bought ARKA Group L.P. on 9 March 2026 for USD 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired, which the September 2026 quarterly report restates at USD 2,637.7 million after a USD 5.0 million working-capital refund, and funded it from increased borrowings and cash on hand. The new debt was a USD 800.0 million Term Loan B-2 amended onto the Term Loan B on the closing date, with the same guarantees and collateral, and USD 500.0 million of additional 2033 Notes issued on 12 March 2026 at a premium for net proceeds of USD 516.5 million that repaid revolver borrowings; a USD 1,300.0 million bridge commitment dated 19 December 2025 was never drawn and was terminated at closing. The notes are senior unsecured and subordinated to the senior secured facilities, with a repurchase right at 101% after a change of control accompanied by a ratings decline. The consequence for creditors is a larger secured term loan layer ahead of the notes, with sources and uses and pro forma leverage not printed.

## Request

CACI INTERNATIONAL INC /DE/ (issuer id caci), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. The scope is the integrated fundamental credit view built on Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance and the seven supplied issuer documents. It states no rating, security recommendation, covenant conclusion or recovery view.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

CACI's fundamental credit profile is solid but leveraged: federal revenue, rising margins and strong cash conversion support 3.69x net leverage that is falling, while a budget delay combined with a fixed-price cost overrun is the primary downside.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4

Liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million against USD 46.75 million of scheduled amortisation and no large maturity before fiscal 2031 gives time to absorb that downside, but the liquidity rests on one revolver, and the receivables programme that adds cash flow is at its cap and ends on 18 December 2026 unless renewed. Covenant headroom and ratings are not established, so the view is a fundamental one.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 20–21; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 89; calculation C25
### Key findings

- The business is stable in demand but depends on one customer family. Federal contracts were 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue and revenue grew 10.89% to USD 9,567.78 million, of which 7.2% was organic, so cash flow follows appropriations; organic growth slowed to 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter, and USD 6.2 billion of USD 34.0 billion of backlog is funded.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 20; calculation C1

- Margins are improving and cost-plus work protects them, but the mix is moving away from cost-plus work. The EBITDA margin rose to 12.3% in fiscal 2026 from 11.2% and reached 13.3% in the September 2026 quarter, while fixed-price work reached 33.2% of revenue; a fall of 1.00 percentage points in the margin on trailing revenue would remove USD 97.55 million of EBITDA and lift net leverage to 4.01x.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-05_fy26-q4caci20260805ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10; calculation C3; calculation C4

- Cash conversion is strong, but fiscal 2026 had help from tax timing and receivable sales. Issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 735.43 million, 62.65% of EBITDA, on operating cash flow of USD 886.71 million against USD 547.01 million; deferred income taxes swung by USD 172.45 million, 19.45% of operating cash flow, and sales of receivables added USD 44.62 million. In the September 2026 quarter operating cash flow fell to USD 161.31 million from USD 171.07 million as collection days rose to 59 from 56.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 67, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C5

- Leverage rose with the ARKA acquisition and is now falling, but the ratios mix periods. Net leverage moved from 2.91x before the acquisition to 4.63x at 31 March 2026, then to 4.01x at 30 June 2026 and 3.69x at 30 September 2026; interest cover is 5.60x on cash interest and 4.21x against the annualised interest charge, falling to 3.88x if the margin also falls by 1.00 percentage points, so both ratios depend on the part-year ARKA effect.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4

- Liquidity is the strongest support. Liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million is 35.82 times the USD 46.75 million of scheduled amortisation, the next large maturity is USD 1,706.75 million in the year to 30 June 2031, and the revolver is USD 605.00 million drawn; the risk is concentration, since the undrawn revolver is the only committed source of liquidity and USD 160.72 million of collections owed to the receivables purchaser is a liability that net debt does not count.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 21; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C6

- Refinancing capacity looks adequate on recent market access but is untested by ratings or covenants. CACI placed USD 1,500.00 million of 2033 Notes within ten months and extended its credit facility, 69.16% of principal debt is floating and swaps cover 41.61% of that, so each 1% move in rates changes annual interest by about USD 20.4 million; no rating or covenant level is supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 88–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 22; calculation C7; calculation C8

- Financial policy is moderate but unverified. No dividend has ever been paid, repurchases fell in fiscal 2026 and no sponsor exists, but acquisitions are debt-funded and the executed debt documents that would show capacity for distributions are not in the set.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 104–105
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a solid profile is that fiscal 2026 cash flow was helped by items that may not repeat: deferred income taxes swung by USD 172.45 million, income tax expense exceeded cash taxes paid by USD 75.38 million, and sales of receivables added USD 44.62 million to operating cash flow, so free cash flow could fall short of the issuer's guidance of at least USD 900 million for fiscal 2027 if those effects reverse; organic growth has slowed to 2.1% and the fixed-price share is rising. The view would weaken if the September 2026 collection days of 59 rise further, if the receivables programme lapses on 18 December 2026, or if a continuing resolution delays awards against the small funded backlog. It would strengthen if free cash flow reaches the guided floor while net leverage keeps falling from 3.69x and the executed debt documents show tight distribution limits.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 67, 85; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C5
### Limitations

- The fiscal 2027 guidance for revenue and free cash flow is not restated on the new calendar basis after the fiscal year change, so the guided free cash flow cannot be mapped to the transition period or to calendar 2027, and the monitoring floor built on it may move.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

- No rating, covenant level or dated market price supports the refinancing assessment, so refinancing capacity rests on recent issuance and the maturity ladder alone, which keeps the view at an adequate profile rather than a confident one.

- The tax-timing and receivable-sale effects on cash flow are read from statement lines, not from a management bridge, so the share of fiscal 2026 free cash flow that is repeatable is a range and not a point estimate.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 67
- Program, segment and customer-level margins are not disclosed, so the margin sensitivity is a trailing-total estimate and cannot show which contracts would carry an overrun.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 52, 98
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Federal demand is large and broad: revenue of USD 9,567.78 million in fiscal 2026 came from agencies across defense, intelligence and civilian missions, and USD 34.0 billion of backlog gives visibility, so a single program loss does not threaten debt service. Cash conversion is high: free cash flow was 62.65% of EBITDA and the issuer guides to at least USD 900 million in fiscal 2027, which funds deleveraging. Liquidity is large against near-term maturities: USD 1,674.39 million against USD 46.75 million of amortisation. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditures of 1.11% of revenue, so cash flow is not absorbed by plant. Financial policy is conservative on distributions: no dividend has been paid and repurchases fell to USD 17.08 million in fiscal 2026.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 46, 67; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C2

Weaknesses. Customer concentration leaves cash flow exposed to appropriations and shutdowns, with only USD 6.2 billion of backlog funded. Fixed-price work at 33.2% of revenue leaves cost overruns with CACI. Debt-funded acquisitions raised net leverage from 2.91x to a high of 4.63x, and goodwill and intangibles are 72.40% of total assets, so recovery rests on contract cash flows. Working capital is absorbing cash as collection days rise, and the receivables programme that offset it is at its cap and has a stated end on 18 December 2026. Covenant levels, ratings and ownership detail are not supplied.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 20; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66, 85; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Credit-relevant company description

CACI is a holding company whose subsidiaries sell Technology, such as software-defined, cyber, electronic warfare and space solutions, and Expertise, meaning cleared technical staff, to national security customers. Technology was 58.4% of fiscal 2026 revenue and Domestic Operations 96.8%, with a small U.K. and European business. The model supports cash-flow visibility through multi-year contracts and a backlog of USD 34.0 billion, but renewals and funding are decided year by year by the customer, so visibility is longer than the funding behind it, and the business has grown through acquisitions that added debt.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–9; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_fy26-q4caci20260805ex991.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Ownership and group structure

CACI is a listed holding company with one class of common stock and no sponsor or controlling holder identified; the guarantor group, ownership percentages and board independence are in documents that are not supplied. With no sponsor there is no sponsor extraction or support to assess, and financial policy rests on the Board: no dividend has ever been paid, repurchases are small, and acquisitions are debt-funded. Creditor alignment is therefore judged from conduct, which is moderate, and not from structure, which is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 103–105
### Revenue durability

Revenue grew 12.64% in fiscal 2025 and 10.89% in fiscal 2026, with organic growth of 7.2% in fiscal 2026 and 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter. The Department of War supplied 53.6% of revenue, the Intelligence Community 24.6% and federal civilian agencies 17.4%, and the ten largest contracts were 22.5% of revenue. The revenue is predictable in aggregate but concentrated and budget-dependent: continuing resolutions and the shutdown from 1 October 2025 to 12 November 2025 delay awards, and only USD 6.2 billion of USD 34.0 billion of backlog is funded. The credit implication is that a funding delay moves cash flow before it moves covenants or ratings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 12, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18, 20
### Margin resilience

The EBITDA margin was 11.2% in fiscal 2025, 12.3% in fiscal 2026 and 13.3% in the September 2026 quarter. Cost-plus-fee contracts, 52.8% of revenue in the quarter, pass cost inflation to the customer, while fixed-price work, 33.2%, leaves overruns with CACI; direct costs fell to 64.6% of revenue on mix, and indirect costs rose to 22.2% on a larger labor base. Margins can be defended against volume pressure because labor is variable with contract volume, but an adverse fixed-price outcome would not be passed on. A fall of 1.00 percentage points on trailing revenue removes USD 97.55 million of EBITDA.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-05_fy26-q4caci20260805ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C3
### Free cash flow conversion

Capital expenditures were 1.11% of revenue in fiscal 2026, so most EBITDA reaches cash flow before interest and tax. Issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 735.43 million, 62.65% of EBITDA, but operating cash flow of USD 886.71 million included a USD 172.45 million swing in deferred income taxes and USD 44.62 million from receivable sales, and cash taxes paid were USD 75.38 million below income tax expense. In the September 2026 quarter working capital absorbed cash, with days sales outstanding at 59. Cash flow is durable in direction but fiscal 2026 overstates the repeatable level by the tax and receivable-sale effects, whose size cannot be fixed from the filings alone.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 66–67, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C5
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is high: the company states that it competes against many firms, some larger, with no dominant competitor and a relatively small share of its addressable market, so re-competes can be lost, which would show first in backlog and awards. Non-traditional entrants in cloud, cyber and satellite operations raise entry pressure, and agencies that perform services for themselves are an indirect substitute. Buyer power is strong because the government sets contract terms and can terminate for convenience, although terminations have been rare. Supplier power sits mainly in cleared labor, where competition for skilled staff is intense and limits cost control. The credit effect is limited pricing power and a reliance on win rates and contract mix.
### Macro and policy factors

Policy is the dominant external factor. Defense appropriations of USD 838.7 billion were enacted for the government's 2026 fiscal year and mandatory funding of about USD 156 billion for defense became available outside annual appropriations, which supports demand regardless of continuing resolutions. Economic exposure is mainly interest rates, since most debt is floating. The credit effect is demand support from defense funding against timing risk from shutdowns, which interrupted government operations from 1 October to 12 November 2025.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: federal scale, cash conversion of 62.65% of EBITDA, low capital intensity, large liquidity and no dividend history. Weaknesses: concentration, fixed-price drift, acquisition leverage, goodwill-heavy assets and a capped receivables programme. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: defense funding and the guided free cash flow of at least USD 900 million, which could pay down debt. Threats that could weaken it: a prolonged shutdown or continuing resolution, a large fixed-price overrun, integration problems at ARKA and a rise in floating rates.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 22
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is a support: revenue of USD 9,567.78 million and a margin that reached 13.3% give shock absorption. Competitive advantage and diversification are average: customers are many agencies but one government, and the company reports no dominant position. Cost and capex flexibility is a support, with capital expenditures of 1.11% of revenue and a labor-based cost base. Margin stability is average because the mix is shifting toward fixed-price work. Free cash flow stability is average because fiscal 2026 had tax and receivable-sale help. Liquidity is a support at USD 1,674.39 million. Ability to refinance is average because recent issuance is strong but ratings and covenants are not supplied. Financial policy and governance is average: distributions are minimal but acquisitions are debt-funded and structural governance is not established. The trend is improving leverage from a high of 4.63x at 31 March 2026 to 3.69x; the main constraints are concentration and fixed-price risk; the key missing datapoints are covenant levels, ratings, ownership detail and ARKA pro forma earnings.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 10; calculation C4; calculation C6
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the issuer raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to USD 10,700 million to USD 10,900 million and guides to free cash flow of at least USD 900 million, supported by a 2.0x book-to-bill in the quarter and defense funding; that supports deleveraging if working capital cooperates. Headwinds are collection days at 59, a fixed-price share of 33.2%, slower organic growth of 2.1% and the end of the receivables term on 18 December 2026. Over three to five years the issuer states it is on track for its three-year targets, but the filings give no detail, so the medium-term view rests on the maturity ladder, with USD 1,706.75 million due in the year to 30 June 2031, and on continued defense funding.
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a continuing resolution or shutdown, as occurred from 1 October 2025, that delays task order awards while a fixed-price program overruns. The first operational break is slower revenue conversion from a backlog of which only USD 6.2 billion is funded, with the overrun cutting the margin. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA and weaker cash conversion; a fall of 1.00 percentage points in the margin on trailing revenue removes USD 97.55 million of EBITDA, lifts net leverage to 4.01x and cuts cover to 3.88x against the annualised interest charge, while collection days of 59 and a capped receivables programme absorb cash. The liquidity consequence is a draw on the revolver from USD 1,674.39 million of liquidity; the leverage consequence is a return to the level of 30 June 2026. Management levers are repurchases, which are small, acquisitions, which can be paused, and capital expenditures of only 1.11% of revenue. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because liquidity is 35.82 times scheduled amortisation, but covenant headroom is not established. Observable triggers are collection days above 59, a book-to-bill below 1.0x and free cash flow below USD 900 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16, 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6
### Overall credit view

Overall, CACI presents an adequate business profile supported by federal scale, broad agency demand, cash conversion of 62.65% of EBITDA and large liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, a rising fixed-price share and acquisition debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because fiscal 2026 benefited from tax timing and receivable sales. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on federal funding continuity, leverage continuing to fall from 3.69x and the November 2030 revolver and Term Loan maturities. The primary downside path is a budget delay combined with a fixed-price overrun. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, ratings, the proxy statement and ARKA pro forma earnings. Top risk: federal funding delay.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 88–89
